dedupe_keys.name: im3 hourly us electricity demand projections with and without epri data centre growth 2022 to 2040

description: This dataset from Pacific Northwest National Laboratory's Integrated Multisector Multiscale Modeling (IM3) project gives scenarios of hourly total electricity demand for 54 balancing authorities of the United States from 2022 to 2040, with and without projected loads from data centres. The base loads come from four IM3 weather and socioeconomic scenarios (rcp45hotter and rcp85hotter with SSP3 and SSP5), documented in Burleyson et al. 2024 and 2025. Data centre loads were layered on from the Electric Power Research Institute's 2024 report 'Powering Intelligence', whose annual state-level projections for low (3.71 percent a year), moderate (5 percent), high (10 percent) and higher (15 percent) growth are included, converted to flat 8,760-hour loads and spread across balancing authorities. Coverage: the contiguous United States by balancing authority. Format and access: CSV and XLSX files through OSTI and the MSD-LIVE repository, free of charge. Caveats: data centre load is assumed flat through the day and year; state-to-balancing-authority allocation is simple; scenarios, not forecasts. Simulation uses: stress on power systems from data centre growth, capacity planning and interdependency studies between digital and power infrastructure under climate scenarios. Related records: the Virginia data centre facility dataset and the IM3 grid stress datasets of the energy piece.
